where coefficients $a \dots h$ are determined by the corner values and coordinates [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the input grid consists of hexahedral cells bounded by eight vertices (corners) with associated data values. It further explains that interpolation schemes (like trilinear interpolation) estimate the function value at a point P based on the known values at the corners of the identified cell. The mathematical formula provided for trilinear interpolation ($F(P) = a + bx + cy + dz + exy + fzx + gy^2 + hz^2$ or similar linear combinations depending on the specific expansion, though the text cuts off, the context implies coefficients are derived from the corner values to define the function within the cell) confirms that coefficients are determined by the corner values. While the claim mentions 'coordinates', in the context of interpolation within a specific cell defined by vertex coordinates and values, the coefficients of the interpolating polynomial are indeed determined by the corner values (and implicitly the geometry/coordinates of those corners to map the local space). The evidence supports that the method relies on corner values to determine the estimation (coefficients) for points within the cell.
